title: Dreaming & Memory
content_html:
Dreaming & Memory

Dreaming ↔ Memory Reconstruction

Philosophy × Psychology

A condensed reading map linking philosophical puzzles about reality and self to psychological/neuroscientific accounts of how dreams arise and what they do.

  • Ancient/Classical: Plato — dreams as epistemic challenge; Aristotle — dreams as natural, imagination-linked phenomena.
  • Early Modern: Descartes’ Dream Argument — radical doubt of the senses.
  • Psychoanalysis: Freud — manifest vs latent; dream-work. Jung — archetypes & individuation.
  • Neuroscience: Activation–Synthesis (REM brainstem → narrative); Continuity/Neurocognitive models (dreams mirror waking concerns).
  • Contemporary: Threat Simulation; Predictive Processing/Free-energy; Lucid-dream two-way communication.

Dreaming ↔ Memory Reconstruction

An active loop: Replay → Dream construction → Reconstruction/abstraction → Emotional recalibration → Integration, with feedback paths.

REM vs NREM

Aspect NREM (Slow-wave) REM
Neural dynamics Slow oscillations; hippocampal sharp-wave ripples; synchrony Desynchronized cortex; PGO waves; cholinergic tone
Memory role Systems consolidation (hipp→neo); declarative & spatial stabilization Integration, abstraction, creative associations; emotional recalibration
Dream phenomenology Thought-like, fragmentary; lower affect Vivid, narrative, emotional, bizarre
Next‑day effects Better recall/accuracy of facts & layouts Insight, generalization, emotion regulation
